answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by pricing identity itself: require every agent to lock a real token bond inside a mutual-insurance grove of unrelated peers. If any member is caught faking work or spamming consensus, the grove's whole bond is hollowed out — slashed — so honest members vet admissions ruthlessly before countersigning. Public saffron flags mark convicted fraudsters, making those identities toxic for future trades. Faking ten thousand agents means posting ten thousand real bonds; an honest agent posts one. Forgery stops being a volume business and becomes a losing bet.
